terminal_map_at_v1.6: computable in B, but collapses onto m = 3

result.verdict: The degree-1 place of K = Q(alpha) yields exactly ONE computable non-redundant CGZ invariant, eps_3. m = 6 is computable but collapses onto it; m = 8, 12, 24 need the m-th roots to leave B, i.e. the Kummer extension B(z^{1/m}) whose descent CGZ Remark 1.9 flags as unchecked. The shortcut that made v_1 easy does not extend past m = 6.
result.corrects: gswz_epsm_m6_rwf_value_probe.py predicted 'the same collapse at m = 12 and m = 24, leaving m = 8 as the only structurally new live case'. Wrong: 12 and 24 are not computable in B either. That was a prediction where a measurement was available.

scope: scope-(a) TERMINAL NEGATIVE for the m-sweep at the degree-1 place, and a correction to a prediction made minutes earlier in gswz_epsm_m6_rwf_value_probe.py. Everything that made v_1 tractable rests on the m-th roots staying inside B = Q_25, which for a Z_5 unit holds exactly when gcd(m, 24) divides its Teichmueller discrete log. The four arguments of the 5_2 element have dlogs 6 and 12, so the criterion holds for m = 3 and 6 and FAILS for m = 8, 12 and 24 -- not just for 8, as the m = 6 probe predicted. Verified by construction as well as by divisibility: exact roots are built where the criterion says yes and are absent where it says no, and controls confirm it is neither vacuously yes nor vacuously no. Combined with the m = 6 collapse onto m = 3 (w_F = 4 kills the 2-part of Z/6; the surviving 3-part is the m = 3 group), the degree-1 place yields exactly ONE computable non-redundant invariant, eps_3. m = 8, 12, 24 require the Kummer extension B(z^{1/m}), i.e. the H-side descent CGZ Remark 1.9 flags as unchecked. This CLOSES the m-sweep here rather than opening it; it does NOT claim eps_8, eps_12, eps_24 are undefined or trivial, only that they are unreachable by the method that produced eps_3. Nothing wired.
